Thresh-task macBP gamma & odor-condition spectrograms

Zelano Lab — threshTask analysis

2026-07-01

1. Methods

Data. Thresh-task intracranial/scalp recordings, preprocessed to 500 Hz (high-pass 0.03 Hz, low-pass ~Nyquist, notch 60/120/180 Hz). Analysis channels are the bipolar macro pairs macBP1..5 (count varies; sessions without any macBP are excluded). Sessions are grouped as DupiS1 / DupiS2 / DupiS3 (Dupi study, recording session 1/2/3) and Control (all non-Dupi thresh sessions).

Design. Each thresh session is 45 single-sniff trials. Every trial delivers one of three odorants — air (clean-air control), low, or med (two PEA concentrations) — and the participant makes one cued sniff per trial. The sniff onset (finalOnset, respiration-phase refined) is the response event; TTL.start (= sniff − 2 s @500 Hz) is the pre-sniff marker used as the baseline anchor.

FOOOF (Task 1). Per session, each macBP PSD (FieldTrip ft_freqanalysis, mtmfft, 2 s segments, 50% overlap, piped in via EEGLAB eeglab2fieldtrip) was parameterized with FOOOF over 2–58 Hz with a knee aperiodic term (cfg.output = fooof_aperiodic / fooof_peaks; brainstorm process_fooof). The gamma band is 30–58 Hz. Before selecting bestMac, each channel’s trial-rejection rate is estimated (fraction of TTL.start epochs flagged noisy by the relative sharp-deflection rule, below); channels exceeding 30% are excluded from bestMac consideration, preventing a high-noise channel whose broadband artifact mimics a gamma peak from being selected. Among the remaining (clean) channels: bestMac is the channel with the largest periodic gamma peak; if no clean channel has a fitted gamma peak we fall back to the largest flattened (PSD ÷ aperiodic) power; if all channels exceed 30% we select the least-noisy one (selectionMethod = 'allNoisy_leastBad'). The selectionMethod and per-channel rejRate columns record the outcome.

Spectrograms (z-score method), split by odor condition. For each session’s bestMac, per-trial time-frequency power was obtained from EEGLAB newtimef (Morlet, 100 log-spaced freqs 2–120 Hz; single-trial alltfX → |·|²), locked to the sniff onset (finalOnset). Trials were split three ways by odor condition (behDat.type ∈ {air, low, med}), all finalOnset-locked. Power was normalized with a bootstrap permutation z-score (myChanZscore): per frequency, each condition’s finalOnset epochs are z-scored against those same trials’ pre-start baseline — the −700…−200 ms window relative to TTL.start, appended per-trial before z-scoring (exactly as cue z-scores finalOnset against its trialStart baseline). Because start = sniff − 2 s, this baseline sits ~2.2–2.7 s before the sniff, a clean pre-stimulus reference. All three condition maps use one identical baseline definition; they differ only in which trials feed them (~15 trials each, minus noise). Display window −1000…+3000 ms; the mean respiration trace (chosen rsp channel, flipped) is overlaid (black line, right axis). Group means (Task 4) average the per-subject z maps (and respiration) within each group × condition on one shared color scale.

Noise rejection (relative sharp-deflection rule). Sharp deflections are detected relative to each channel’s own variability, so a uniformly high-amplitude channel is not rejected merely for being high-amplitude. For the bestMac trace we compute the sliding 10 ms max-to-min range d and robust-z it over the whole recording: zd = (d − median(d)) / (1.4826·MAD(d)) — how many robust-SDs a given 10 ms swing sits above that channel’s typical 10 ms swing. A 10 ms window is an event if zd > K, and a trial (TTL.start-locked epoch −1.75…+5.75 s) is flagged noisy if it contains any event. The threshold K = 10 was calibrated once across the dataset (thresh_calibrate_noise) to drop >0 % and ≤20 % of trials; the same K applies to every session. Noisy trials are drawn in red on singleTrialRawMac.png and excluded from all spectrograms and from the gamma analysis.

6. Time-resolved gamma (FOOOF over epochs, per odor condition)

Methods. For each session’s bestMac, per odor condition, Morlet power (2–58 Hz, 100 linear freqs) was computed on that condition’s noise-clean finalOnset-locked trials, then averaged over trials and into ten sequential 250 ms windows spanning −500…+2000 ms. FOOOF (same settings as the overall channel fit) was applied to each window; the largest 30–58 Hz periodic peak per window is recorded in threshTask_gammaEpochs.csv (with a cond column). A condition with fewer than 8 clean trials in a session is skipped for that session. “Channel-centered” = each window’s gamma peak frequency minus that channel’s overall gamma peak (from §3).

6.3 Channel-centered gamma peak frequency across epochs

Group average per condition (bold) with individual sessions as lighter connected dots.

6.4 Does gamma peak frequency change over epochs / condition? (LME per group)

Linear mixed-effects model gammaPeakFreq ~ epoch * cond + (1|subject), fit within each group; falls back to ~ epoch + cond if the interaction model is singular or fails. Epochs with no FOOOF-detected gamma peak are treated as missing. The epoch slope is Hz per 250 ms window; cond terms are Hz offsets from the low reference condition.

LME: gamma peak frequency ~ epoch * cond + (1|subject), per group.
